oob_join.note: lS passes an empty object as the OOB table to Y4, so designation/name are never used: every label is derived from the unit_id

label_uniqueness.note: label text always derives from unit_id (cx); OOB designation/name is never used because lS passes an empty object to Y4

side_prefix_suspects.rule: unit_id starts with U- (drawn Union blue) but ends in a Confederate state code (AL, TX, NC, ...)
side_prefix_suspects.evidence: Computed from ids; whether these are authoring errors is Unknown until a historian checks them

hitFlash.rule: uF flags a unit when its row at the new tick has lower strength than its row at the previous tick (Qx = now + 1000 ms); both rows must exist
hitFlash.note: with a 1-tick step only the adjacent pairs can flash; at 2x and faster the app jumps several ticks per frame and compares rows at those two ticks only

orientation.consequence: long axis of every filled tile is parallel to the facing direction; placement_schema.json says Line of Battle extends perpendicular to bearing
orientation.schemaText: Line of Battle extends perpendicular to bearing.

tile_spec.evidence: Computed from the shipped draw routine lS (extracted from the bundle and run), Measured on the page by the canvas probe; specimen sheet = the same routine run on synthetic placements

canvas.element: one full-size 2D canvas, z-index 10, above the Mapbox canvas; backing store = CSS pixels (no devicePixelRatio scaling)
canvas.baselinePointerEvents: auto (swallows mouse pan and wheel, measured)
canvas.r1cPointerEvents: none (map receives input, clicks come from the map click event)

redrawsOnMapMove.r1c: yes, via GtbgRepaint on move and resize

shapes.Deployed/Limbered Artillery or id contai: outline rectangle 2 px in side colour plus a centre line half the width
shapes.Skirmish Line: dashed line (4 px dash, 3 px gap), 2 px, side colour
shapes.all other dispositions: filled rectangle in side colour, 1 px border, opacity 0.88 (1.0 when selected)

colours.engaged_glow: white shadowBlur 8, alpha 0.4 + 0.6 * |sin(t/300)| (about 1.06 Hz), reduced to a constant under reduced motion in R1c only

tile_spec.rotation: rotate((bearing - 90) deg): the long axis is parallel to the facing direction for every tile (451 of 451 checked); placement_schema.json says Line of Battle extends perpendicular to bearing
tile_spec.disposition_badge: a 7 px circle (radius 3.5, 1 px black ring) drawn 7 px above the tile centre in screen space, never rotated; it is the only difference between Line of Battle, Charging Line, Chaotic Retreat, Line of March, Reserve and Bivouac tiles, and between mounted and dismounted cavalry and deployed and limbered artillery

label.box: rgba(0,0,0,0.72), padding 3 x 2 px, centred 13 px above the tile centre, text #aaccff (Union) or #ffbbaa (Confederate)
label.rules: none below zoom 12 (14 on the phone) unless selected; zoom 12-13.99: first 6 characters of the id label; 14-16.49: full id label; 16.5+: id label + strength; font bold 8 px (<14), 9 px (14-16), 10 px (>=16 or selected)
label.source_of_text: always derived from unit_id; OOB designation is never used (an empty object is passed to the label function)

tile_spec.relaxation: 8 passes of pairwise pushing on unrotated boxes (width/2+2 by a 12 px band), displaced tiles get a 0.5 px leader line when moved more than 3 px; runs every redraw from scratch

trails.canvas: z-index 8, intrinsic size 300 x 150 in both builds (never resized): trail segments only exist inside the top-left 300 x 150 px, 3.7 percent of a 1440 x 852 map

minimum_zoom_reality.note: jumpTo zoom 11 on the 1440 px desktop was measured to land at 12.04; minZoom 11 is only reachable on narrow screens

input_and_state.hit_rule: click -> unproject -> nearest unit by degrees among the cells within 0.002 deg of the click (about 220 m north-south, 170 m east-west) of the TRUE positions of the current tick; no pixel radius, no use of the drawn (displaced) tile; a click with no candidate deselects
input_and_state.baseline_hit_note: in production the same click code runs (identical text in both bundles); real clicks at the tile centre selected it in 4 of 4 zooms (first input run); off-centre clicks follow the same rule

timing.evidence: Measured: real Chrome 155 (headless=new, real GPU), rAF cadence of the page, one entry per unit-canvas redraw, duration of the rAF callback that drew, PerformanceObserver long tasks (>50 ms). Absolute fps and ms depend on this machine; the pattern (cadence bimodal at 16.7 and 33.4 ms in dense scenes) is what matters.

motion.evidence: Computed by replaying the shipped Ed/y1/F4/lS code (extracted from the bundle) with the REAL rAF timestamps of each browser run. Validation: for 3 real R1c runs (487, 365 and 485 frames) the replay reproduced every frame (tile count, sum of x, y, angle, width, label count) with zero difference.
motion.baseline_note: the interpolation, easing, hop and snap-back code is byte-identical in the baseline bundle (F4, z4, y1 apart from the carry-forward cache); only the unit SET differs (stale cache), so the motion numbers apply to the units the baseline draws; the baseline cannot be replayed exactly because its cache depends on which ticks were visited

snapBacks.note: a unit that is interpolating between keyframes of ticks f and f+1 is drawn LATER on its path than in the previous frame (same f, smaller fraction): the stale tick snapshot in Ed

smoothFrames.note: px/s^2 and px/s^3 of the true (projected) position on runs of 3+ consecutive frames inside one interpolated tick (same keyframe pair, fraction increasing, not the boundary frame); constant-speed motion would give 0

afterSnapBackFrame.note: the frame after a snap-back: the unit jumps forward again

overlap.evidence: Computed: the shipped lS drawn for every displayed state (carry-forward, one per keyframe tick, 188 states standing for all 675 ticks) into a recording context with real Chrome text widths; geometry census of the recorded tiles, dots and labels
overlap.method: pairs = tile bodies (rotated rectangles) that overlap by more than 0.5 px; hidden share = share of a tile body covered by LATER tiles or by OTHER units labels (labels are painted after all tiles); dot hidden = at least half of the badge disc covered by others; label illegible = more than 30 percent covered by a later label
overlap.caution_zoom_11_12: the desktop camera cannot go below zoom 12.04 on 1440 px (maxBounds), so z11 and z12 columns on desktop are virtual

hotspots.overlap_clusters: see topClustersByPlace per zoom (place = nearest key location of data/terrain.json); clusters include stale carry-forward units
hotspots.freshDefinition: units whose latest keyframe is at most 12 ticks (1 h) old

unverified: Absolute frame times and fps were measured on one machine (Intel Core Ultra 7 265H, Arc Pro 140T, Chrome 155, headless=new): a low-end phone will be slower, and no real phone was tested; the 4x CPU throttle runs are an emulation
The phone numbers use Chrome device emulation (390x844, DPR 3, touch) on the desktop, not a real handset; the canvas size check (390 px backing store at DPR 3) is exact, the speed is not

The baseline (production) motion cannot be replayed exactly because its carry-forward cache depends on every tick it has ever drawn; baseline statements about the unit set come from real runs (state_after_actions), baseline motion statements rest on the byte-identical interpolation code
The side-prefix suspects (U- ids with Confederate state codes) are inferred from the id text; a historian has not checked them
Whether hop distances such as 5.7 km in 5 minutes are authoring choices or errors in the placements is Unknown; they are reported as data, not corrected

Hit-test model versus real clicks: 20 of 21 real clicks (R1c, zoom 12.04, 14 and 17) selected exactly what the model predicted; the one difference is a click 400 px from a tile at zoom 12.04. The baseline click code is identical but its tile set is wrong, so only the centre click was tried there
No hover reaction was found in the code and none was observed; touch interaction (tap select, 300 ms tap rule) was read from code only
Mapbox basemap tiles were not part of the measurement subject; their GPU cost is included in the page frame times but not separated
